svg.title: A client with Addison disease has had vomiting and diarrhea for two days and has been unable to keep down her hydrocortisone. Blood pressure 78/46, heart rate 124, glucose 54 mg/dL, sodium 128 mEq/L, potassium 5.9 mEq/L.
svg.desc: Missing steroid doses during a vomiting illness is the classic trigger for addisonian crisis, and the picture is hypotension, hypoglycemia, low sodium and high potassium. Treatment is IV hydrocortisone with aggressive isotonic fluid, given together and immediately. Oral steroid cannot be absorbed or given fast enough, and adding potassium to a level of 5.9 mEq/L would be dangerous.
